title: Nested Hashes and Structured Data
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of nested hashes and structured data in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply nested hashes and structured data in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to representing json-like data and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Nested Hashes and Structured Data through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding nested hashes and structured data helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Nested Hashes and Structured Data helps you reason about nested objects. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Nested objects. Then connect it to Safe access to nested values. The remaining syllabus points—Representing JSON-like data—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports nested hashes and structured data. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for nested hashes and structured data using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Representing JSON-like data), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain nested hashes and structured data, identify its place in hashes, sets, and ranges, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
